definitions.gloss: to accompany, to go together with
definitions.explanation: To go along with someone to the same destination, often in a professional, formal, or supportive capacity.

examples.japanese: {通訳|つうやく}が{同行|どうこう}する。
{出張|しゅっちょう}に{部下|ぶか}を{同行|どうこう}させた。
examples.english: I had my subordinate accompany me on the business trip.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}{官|かん}が{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}の{自宅|じたく}まで{同行|どうこう}し、{家宅捜索|かたくそうさく}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: Police officers accompanied the suspect to their home and conducted a house search.

notes:
A compound of {同|どう} (same, together) and {行|こう} (go). More formal than {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}く. Often used in business, travel, and official contexts where someone goes along in a professional role.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出張|しゅっちょう}に{同行|どうこう}する: to accompany on a business trip
- {取材|しゅざい}に{同行|どうこう}する: to accompany on a news report
- {同行者|どうこうしゃ}: companion, person accompanying
- {同行|どうこう}を{求|もと}める: to request someone's company

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {付|つ}き{添|そ}う: to attend, to escort — implies providing care or support
- {随行|ずいこう}する: to accompany (a superior) — more formal, specifically following a person of higher status
- {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}く: to go together — the casual everyday expression
